lines.text: They knew how to fix it.
Time bent backward, files came through,
future sent warnings with receipts and proof.
Names, dates, damage, every domino mapped,
every little choice and where the timeline cracked.
Decision-makers sitting with tomorrow on screen,
watching whole worlds turn cruel and obscene.
Could’ve changed one choice, could’ve closed one door,
but somebody might lose what they already scored.
So they weighed one life against leverage and rank,
one city against somebody’s money in the bank.
One generation versus one comfortable chair—
then called doing nothing “being measured and fair.”
Everybody had something personal to lose.
So the future kept screaming through holes in the past,
while the people with power kept protecting their ass.
One said, “Fixing this could ruin my life.”
One by one, they protected their side—
and built a universe where nobody survives right.
everybody leaves it for somebody else.
where conscience comes second to cost.
but nobody wanted to personally take the loss.
Branch after branch, the disease gets deep,
promises cheap and the consequences steep.
Every timeline inherits the cowardice before it,
then teaches the next generation to ignore it.
Politician sees truth but election comes first.
Executive sees harm but the quarter looks worse.
Scientist sees danger but the funding might vanish.
Judge knows the wound but says, “Not my jurisdiction to manage.”
Neighbor hears screaming, turns television loud.
Whole damn planet learns to disappear in a crowd.
Nobody wakes up planning evil at dawn—
they just protect their little piece while the whole thing goes wrong.
That’s the terrifying part, that’s the twist in the knife:
hell doesn’t always need monsters destroying your life.
Sometimes hell is reasonable people who knew,
saying, “Yes, this is awful… but what can **I** do?”
One said, “Someone else can carry the blame.”
Till every branch of reality learned the same game—
save yourself first, let tomorrow burn in flames.
everybody leaves it for somebody else.
where conscience comes second to cost.
but nobody wanted to personally take the loss.
But somewhere there has to be
one branch that breaks the chain.
One hand that signs the paper.
One voice that tells the truth.
One soul willing to lose something
so strangers don’t have to lose.
So send me every timeline, let me study every scar,
show me where we traded human hearts for who we are.
You don’t need to save infinity in one heroic night—
you just stop making selfishness the price of doing right.
Maybe fixing what’s broken means you lose on your side.
If my comfort needs your suffering—
and decides their loss is worth it.
when somebody volunteers to take the loss.
**“I’ll fix it even if it hurts me.”**
